smoke.cmd: node -e (offline conformance check): for each sprints/*.py assert the 7 mandatory header sections (Sprint lineage / Author / Date / DOCTRINE / WHAT THIS SPRINT DOES / OUTPUT / NEXT-SPRINT SPEC) and the '>>> NEXT: write sprint-' trailer; JSON.parse research/jev-velocity.json, moth-fidelity-matrix.json, quantum-chaos-001.json
smoke.verdict: PASS — 5/5 sprint scripts fully conform to the SPRINT-LINEAGE contract; 3/3 JSON artifacts parse
smoke.notes: The sprint scripts themselves were NOT executed: they require API keys (env TYPESAFEAI_KEY etc.) and network calls to api.typesafe.ai / api.deepinfra.com (sprint-jev-001.py:36) — forbidden by lane rules; the contract-check + JSON-parse verification is the honest offline dog-food. Honest negatives found: (1) registry drift — README.md:35-39 lists 4 sprint frames and SPRINT-LINEAGE.md:35-41 lists 2 active lineages, but sprints/ holds 5 scripts (sprint-quantum-001.py is in neither list) — the canon's own law ('the roadmap is the directory') catches the README; (2) a stray nested duplicate directory quilt-research-canons/quilt-research-canons/research/ holds the contribution thesis; (3) sprint outputs reference /workspace/research/ paths (sandbox-local) while the repo copies live in research/.

essence: Research canon documents: sprint-lineage protocol, pre-registered predictions, witnesses declaring successors.

ideas.name: the roadmap is the directory, not memory
ideas.statement: Each sprint script ends with an embedded NEXT-SPRINT SPEC; the next agent reads the bottom of the prior file, writes the next file, runs it, embeds the spec for the third — the chain of files IS the roadmap, which is how the substrate-walker pattern survives a sandbox wipe (SPRINT-LINEAGE.md:9-11, 68-72).

ideas.name: witness over description
ideas.statement: Every artifact is a witness you can verify, not just describe: each sprint is a runnable stdlib+env-keys script whose output lands at a declared path, and each run is a substrate walker in miniature — walks a substrate, emits a witness, declares its successor (README.md:20, 73-76; SPRINT-LINEAGE.md:51-56).

ideas.name: pre-registered, falsifiable, honestly-verdicted
ideas.statement: The method is fixed before running: (1) state a falsifiable hypothesis, (2) design a small experiment on existing fleet + stdlib + APIs, (3) record the verdict, (4) note new questions — and the verdicts are honest including refutation: H1 FALSIFIED then REFINED and the refinement confirmed; quantum-chaos Q1/Q2 FALSIFIED as posed with the control reported beside them (2026-09-24-novel-problems-report.md:15, 23-31; research/quantum-chaos-001.json verdict).

ideas.name: canon-promotion velocity as a measured gate
ideas.statement: The JEV oracle is the canon-promotion gate, and the gate itself is measured: 5 questions × 20 trials compute 'first stable trial' (all remaining values within ±0.05 of mean); canon should stabilize FAST (don't ask 12 times when the first call says yes at p≥0.85) and speculation should stabilize SLOW (don't promote a 0.55 reading after 3 calls) — the velocity profile is the gate's calibration record (sprint-jev-001.py:9-14; research/jev-velocity.json).

parts.name: dated artifact file
parts.essence: The irreducible representation is a dated file in a git repo — md for arguments, json for measurements, py for runs; discoverability starts at the filesystem, not a memory or a chat log.
parts.evidence: README.md:26-40 (tree); git log (commits e92e88a, 4cd55f1 dated artifacts)

parts.name: JSON measurement records
parts.essence: jev-velocity.json {summary, questions}, moth-fidelity-matrix.json {timestamp, n_samples_per_clip, shots, schemes, clips, matrix}, quantum-chaos-001.json {refusals, quantum, jev, chain, summary, verdict} — machine-readable verdicts with parameters and outcomes co-located.
parts.gate: must parse and carry its own provenance fields

parts.name: sprint script as self-contained run
parts.essence: Each sprint-XXX-NNN.py is std-lib + env keys, re-runnable independently, and lands its output at a declared path — a witness that can be re-executed to re-derive its claim.
outputs: output JSON at the declared path
parts.gate: file must be re-runnable without asking a human anything

parts.name: embedded NEXT-SPRINT SPEC
parts.essence: The mechanism that makes the chain self-extending: the header carries the spec for XXX-(NNN+1) — concrete questions/signals, output location, the 'voice memo' the next header should use, deliverables — plus the mandatory '>>> NEXT:' print trailer.
parts.gate: spec must be specific enough to implement without clarification

parts.name: output archive + lineage table
parts.essence: SPRINT-LINEAGE.md records which lineages are active and where outputs are archived (✅ archived at /workspace/research/…), so the chain's state is queryable from one table rather than by opening every file.
parts.failure_mode: registry drift observed this lane: sprint-quantum-001.py present in sprints/ but absent from both README's tree and SPRINT-LINEAGE's tables

parts.name: the sprint contract
parts.essence: Every sprint-XXX-NNN.py MUST carry the seven header sections (Sprint lineage, Author, Date, DOCTRINE, WHAT THIS SPRINT DOES ≤10 lines, OUTPUT, NEXT-SPRINT SPEC), end with the '>>> NEXT: write sprint-XXX-(NNN+1).py …' print, and NOT spawn sub-agents in its runtime (they routinely return without writing files — direct execution is the reliable path).
parts.gate: all seven sections + trailer present; no sub-agent spawning
parts.failure_mode: non-conformant sprint — the next agent cannot proceed from it (checked this lane: 5/5 conform)

parts.name: inter-relation requirement
parts.essence: The next sprint's voice memo MUST reference the prior sprint's filename so each sprint declares its dependency — the chain is inter-relational, not a pile of independent files.
parts.gate: successor declares its dependency on the predecessor

parts.name: falsifiability method
parts.essence: Fixed method ordering across all problems: falsifiable hypothesis → small experiment on existing fleet + stdlib + available APIs → recorded verdict → new questions surfaced; hypotheses are written BEFORE results and kept visible even when falsified (H1 original shown struck-down beside H1 refined).
parts.gate: hypothesis must be stated before the experiment; verdict must be recorded whatever it is

parts.name: canon-promotion gate velocity
parts.essence: Canon moves FAST (first call yes at p≥0.85 → don't re-ask 12 times), speculation moves SLOW (a 0.55 reading never promotes after 3 calls); the gate's calibration is itself measured (first-stable-trial = index where remaining values stay within ±0.05 of mean).
parts.gate: promotion only after the stability criterion holds
parts.evidence: sprints/sprint-jev-001.py:9-14, 19-21; research/jev-velocity.json (5q × 20 trials, most stable at trial 1)

parts.name: README as agent-facing discoverability layer
parts.essence: The README is written for another agent: what the repo is, a literal how-to-use command block (head the sprint, grep the NEXT-SPRINT SPEC, run it, read the protocol), doctrine, cross-references, status — 'if you're another agent, read this README first'.
parts.failure_mode: README tree drift vs actual directory (honest negative recorded this lane)

parts.name: multi-voice sprint frames
parts.essence: Sprint frames span substrates and voices: jev (Typesafe), moth (quantumaudio fidelity matrix: QSM best continuous r=0.98-1.00, QPAM all-rounder r=0.73-0.87), zai (3-voice chord), deepinfra (6-model chord), quantum (certified-receipts → oracle votes) — each frame the same contract on a different substrate.
parts.failure_mode: chronic API issues stated honestly in the status block (ZAI 429 on rapid-fire, MOTH MSQPAM/MQSM unclear in 0.2.0, Kimi suspended)

parts.name: wipe-survival doctrine
parts.essence: When the sandbox resets, the successor reads the most recent sprint's header (canon-stable today) + next-sprint spec (what to build next), re-runs, validates, writes the next — the pattern survives by writing itself into the filesystem, not into memory.
parts.gate: artifacts + intent-to-continue must both survive the wipe boundary

parts.name: verdict ledger with honest negatives
parts.essence: The canon's evidence layer: H1 FALSIFIED+REFINED (twin brews byte-identical under identical inputs), H2 CONFIRMED at ~85%, H3 CONFIRMED, bonus LIVE CANON-CHORD, and quantum-chaos 'FALSIFIED as posed — Q1=0.14, Q2=0.31, control=0.13' with its calibration against jev velocity recorded — refutation is canon, not shame.
parts.gate: no verdict is discarded for being negative

parts.name: witness-chain fork evidence
parts.essence: The Fork experiment's recorded evidence table: same recipe + same inputs → chains byte-identical (both 8/8 tests); same recipe + different inputs → intact but distinct chains — the result that falsified the original H1, kept as the canon entry for fork semantics.

cells.expr: dated file in git (md | json | py)
script writes JSON to its declared OUTPUT path
NEXT-SPRINT SPEC section + '>>> NEXT:' trailer derived from this run's results
SPRINT-LINEAGE rows: sprint id / substrate / status / output / next
7 header sections + trailer + no-sub-agents (verified 5/5 this lane)
falsifiable statement written BEFORE the experiment
recorded outcome incl. FALSIFIED (H1, quantum-chaos) — never discarded
first_stable_trial = first index where all remaining values within ±0.05 of mean
successor header MUST reference predecessor filename (inter-relation)
read most recent header → re-run → validate → write next (survives the wipe)

layer_logic.0: Dated files in a git repo — md/json/py — are the substrate; the filesystem chain, not agent memory, is the canonical representation.
layer_logic.1: Sprint scripts run, land outputs at declared paths, and embed the next spec: the mechanism is a self-extending chain of executable witnesses.
layer_logic.2: Policy is the contract + the method: seven mandatory header sections, inter-relation to the predecessor, no sub-agents, falsifiable hypothesis before experiment, and a measured canon-promotion velocity gate.
layer_logic.3: Interface = the README as another-agent entrypoint (how-to-run commands, cross-references, honest status) and per-substrate sprint frames speaking the same contract.
layer_logic.4: Evidence = the verdict ledger where refutations are canon (H1, quantum-chaos), fork-semantics evidence tables, calibration JSONs, and the wipe-survival doctrine that makes the chain itself the artifact.
